name: Fennel
tile_uses: The jar, the weekend braise, the halibut salad
why_now: Fennel is a cool-weather vegetable; as the nights drop into the fifties it comes back sweet and crisp. Raw, it's anise-cool and crunchy; cooked slowly, it turns soft and mild.
how_to_choose: No brown bruising or splitting on the outer layers
Fresh, upright fronds; limp fronds mean it's been sitting
buy_this_much: 2 bulbs for the jar every week, plus one for each fennel dish you pick.
price_note: Sold by the bulb. Bigger bulbs are usually the better deal.

flavor_paths.name: Pickled
flavor_paths.description: The month's jar. Cold and sharp beside anything rich.

flavor_paths.name: Braised
flavor_paths.description: With leeks under chicken thighs, until it's soft and sweet.

weekday_uses: Pickled, beside roast chicken and over lentils
Shaved raw with persimmon beside seared halibut
weekend_use: Cut in wedges and braised with leeks under the chicken thighs.
storage: In the fridge, in a bag, for about a week. Cut off the stalks if they don't fit; keep a few fronds.
one_thing_to_learn: Fennel changes completely with heat: raw it's crisp and cool, cooked it goes soft and sweet and loses most of its anise. Someone who doesn't like it raw may love it braised.
